description:
Wire the baked selection inside the prime-field route predicates and at the FieldVec dot-product scratch length.

## Background

The follow-on selector migration design (dev/active/7d824b2f/design.md) governs this task; read it in full. Its §2 fixes the two field kinds and the mechanism rule with four structural read-pattern obligations, §3 gives every field its name, range, default-naming constant, read site and mechanism, §4 names the route reporter and test obligation per family, and §5.3 states the ratified amortisation screening rule and the behaviour-preservation argument (defaults name the in-source constants; observable behaviour unchanged when no profile is installed). Design §3.8, §3.11 and the prime_route and field_vec rows of §4.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: f32_min_prime, f32_min_cols and f64_min_cols resolve through the baked constants inside the const fn predicates (which stay const fn), and dot_chunk_len resolves through its baked constant as the stack-array length, all with arithmetic unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: The prime_gemm_route reporter and both baked witnesses (wired into the CI baked step) pass; the FieldVec dot-product equivalence suite passes unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Rustdoc names the profile fields; existing tests pass unchanged.
title: Cut the prime-route and FieldVec selectors over to the tuning profile
